LEEDS, England, Oct 18 : Manchester United manager Michael Carrick took heart from his team's resilience in Sunday's 1-1 Premier League draw at Leeds United, but his description of the result as a "step forward" underlined how far expectations have fallen during a difficult spell for the club. One win from seven league games has left United languishing in 13th, a stark contrast to last season's third-place finish and evidence that their problems run deeper than a difficult week. Carrick conceded they had fallen short of the quality they are capable of producing, particularly on the ball, but he found encouragement in the discipline and togetherness his players showed in the pressure of a fierce rivalry at Elland Road. "Maybe if you talk about top quality, maybe it wasn't top, top quality I think we are capable of playing," Carrick said. "With the results we've had we weren't quite flowing but there's enough in there to take from it."

The greater significance for Carrick appeared to lie in how United responded to adversity.  After being outplayed in a 1-1 draw with bottom side Tottenham Hotspur last weekend and losing 2-0 at Atletico Madrid in the Champions League, the build-up to Sunday's game was further complicated by Lisandro Martinez publicly criticising the club hierarchy before apologising. Against that backdrop, Carrick placed greater emphasis on structure than style. United were harder to break down, and he praised his players for sticking to their roles and responsibilities in what he described as a tense game that could have gone either way. "It's a bit more than just effort," Carrick said. "It is the way you go about it. The plan. The responsibilities. The roles. I thought the boys took that responsibility on really well for the most part." FAMILIAR SHORTCOMINGS Yet familiar shortcomings remained. United surrendered their lead from a set piece and lacked enough quality in possession to take control of the match, leaving Carrick with another draw rather than the victory his side badly needed. After a week dominated as much by events off the pitch as those on it, however, Carrick was keen to stress that the dressing room remained united. "I suppose you're looking at the togetherness, the spirit, the unit. I don't doubt that within the group," he said. "The way that we went about it today gives me a lot of belief in us moving forward." United head to Como for a Champions League game on Wednesday.

Source: Reuters

LEVERKUSEN, Germany, Oct 18 : Bayer Leverkusen netted a 76th-minute winner through leading scorer Patrik Schick to beat Freiburg 2-1 on Sunday and move into the top four of the Bundesliga standings. Czech striker Schick, who became the first Leverkusen player to score in each of the first six matches of a season, tapped in after superb work from Ibrahim Maza, as his team moved to 13 points, behind Freiburg on goal difference. Bayern Munich, on 14, took over at the top following their 6-1 demolition of RB Leipzig on Saturday. Dortmund are in second place, also on 14. Freiburg, who suffered their first loss of the season across all competitions and face Bayern next week, took a 14th-minute lead through Derry Scherhant, with Germany coach Juergen Klopp watching from the stands. It only lasted five minutes, however, with Ibrahim Maza bagging the equaliser. Neither team had big chances after the break until Maza shook off three markers near the corner line with dazzling skills to cut back for Schick to tap home.

Source: Reuters

BRIGHTON, England, Oct 18 : Diego Gomez produced a stunning halfway-line goal as Brighton & Hove Albion thrashed Crystal Palace 5-0 on Sunday, the Premier League's longest-range strike in nearly nine years. With Brighton 1-0 up following an early own goal from Jaydee Canvot, Gomez spotted Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez off his line in the seventh minute and seized his opportunity from the centre circle. The Paraguayan midfielder took one touch before unleashing a spectacular shot from 51 metres out, leaving the backtracking Benitez desperately flailing his arms as the ball sailed over him and into the back of the net. Gomez's audacious strike was the furthest range goal in the Premier League since Wayne Rooney scored for Everton against West Ham United from 58 metres out in November 2017, according to data firm Opta.

"When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead. When I scored, I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal," Gomez told Sky Sports. "It's about the brotherhood and the intensity. We keep doing this in training and games." Former goalkeeper and BBC pundit Shay Given said he could not blame Benitez for the goal. "We're always talking about sweeper goalkeepers and you've got to be high up for the through ball and the defence playing a high line. I think his position was fine," Given said. "You've just got to take your hat off to Gomez. That is just a brilliant, brilliant goal." Brighton continued to run riot and moved to the top of the scoring charts with 23 goals in seven games this season. They are provisionally second in the standings, five points behind leaders Manchester City.

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 18 : Manchester City held off a spirited comeback from Brighton & Hove Albion on Sunday to secure a 3-2 win that maintained their perfect start to the Women's Super League season, with Chelsea close behind after a convincing win over Tottenham Hotspur. City raced into a 3-0 lead by the 17th minute thanks to a brace from Bunny Shaw and a goal from Niamh Charles, and though Brighton pulled two goals back before the break through Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes, neither side managed to find the net again in the second half. City have 18 points from six games, two ahead of Chelsea after their 6-2 demolition of Tottenham. Lauren James and Ellie Carpenter both scored twice for the Blues against Spurs, who only let in two goals while collecting three wins and a draw in their first four games but have now conceded six in each of their last two league clashes.

Oct 18 : Brighton & Hove Albion's Diego Gomez struck a sensational goal from inside his own half in a 5-0 Premier League rout of Crystal Palace on Sunday that moved them provisionally into second place on 16 points, five behind leaders Manchester City. Manchester United and bitter rivals Leeds United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Elland Road at the end of a turbulent week for the Red Devils in which defender Lisandro Martinez had publicly challenged the club's hierarchy. Leeds are seventh in the table and Manchester United, who have just one win from seven games, are 13th.  Bournemouth beat Sunderland 2-0 for their first league victory of the season to climb to 15th place. Sunderland remained in the drop zone in 19th place.

Champions Arsenal, who began the day with 15 points, travel to Nottingham Forest for Sunday's late game. At the Amex, Brighton got on the scoresheet in the fourth minute through a Jaydee Canvot own goal, before Gomez struck a goal of the season contender three minutes later, robbing Adam Wharton of the ball near the halfway line before taking a touch and firing the ball over keeper Walter Benitez and into the net. "When I got the ball I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead," Gomez told Sky Sports. "When I scored I didn't know where to run or what to do. I was very happy with the goal." Yasin Ayari padded Brighton's lead three minutes later, before Charalampos Kostoulas and Jack Hinshelwood completed the rout after the break. Kostoulas scored just after halftime when Ayari's shot deflected into the Greece international's path, and Hinshelwood struck  in the 84th when Luka Vuskovic's header was scooped off the line by Benitez and he fired home the rebound. MBEUMO GRABS OPENING GOAL Manchester United looked on course for a much-needed victory when Bryan Mbeumo scored in the 35th minute after missing a couple of chances. Mbeumo held off James Justin before tapping in a Youri Tielemans cross from six yards out. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised in the 51st minute, chesting down the ball from a corner before poking home.  "We are slightly disappointed it is just a point," Leeds boss Daniel Farke told Sky. "Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. "We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester United." Manchester defender Martinez retained his place in Michael Carrick's starting lineup despite criticising United's hierarchy following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, questioning the club’s summer investment and singling out technical director Jason Wilcox before later apologising. Bournemouth punished a shaky Sunderland start to take the lead after just six minutes, when Lewis Cook lofted a long ball forward that Evanilson ran on to and squared for Marcus Tavernier to head home from close range. Evanilson scored himself in the 48th minute when the Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Robin Roefs before slotting home left-footed.

Source: Reuters

Egypt is ready to provide Saudi Arabia with the support it needs to defend its security and stability, the presidency said on Sunday (Oct 18), as Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensify their attacks on the world's largest oil exporter. Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi requested an urgent parliament session to authorise the military, one of the Arab world's largest, to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom requested its support. A parliamentary vote had been expected on authorizing the request for military support on Sunday, but discussions were due to continue on Monday, two lawmakers and local media reports said. HOUTHIS RAMP UP ATTACKS ON SAUDI ARABIA The Houthis have in recent days attacked Riyadh's international airport and the state oil giant Saudi Aramco, amid renewed fighting with the Saudi-backed forces of the internationally recognised government following the collapse of a truce.

"Egypt will provide Saudi Arabia with all necessary and possible forms of support to defend its security and stability, protect its resources, territorial integrity and Islamic holy sites," the Egyptian presidency said in a statement. It followed a meeting of Egypt's National Defence Council chaired by Sisi and attended by the parliamentary speaker, the prime minister and the army chief. Sisi said in a speech on Saturday that Egypt would act in accordance with guidance from Saudi King Salman and Crown Prince Mohammed Salman, who visited Sisi on Sep 15, after fighting in Yemen reignited. Egypt and Saudi Arabia are close strategic and economic partners. Saudi Arabia and other oil-rich Gulf states provided Egypt with billions of dollars in aid, central-bank deposits and investments after the military ouster of President Mohamed Morsi in 2013. Egypt had previously joined the Saudi-led coalition that intervened in Yemen in 2015 to support the government against the Houthis, but played a limited combat role.

SEOUL, Oct 18 : Samsung Electronics will use TSMC's 3-nanometre process to produce base dies for Nvidia's next-generation custom high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, the Seoul Economic Daily reported on Sunday. The move would mark the first time Samsung has worked with the Taiwanese contract chipmaker at the HBM manufacturing stage, according to the report. • Nvidia has asked Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technology to use TSMC's process for NVHBM base dies, and sixth-generation DRAM technology for its core dies, the newspaper said, citing industry sources. • NVHBM, unveiled in August, integrates Nvidia's custom memory controller into the base die and is aimed at standardising implementation across multiple memory suppliers, according to the company.

SHANGHAI, Oct 18 : Alejandro Davidovich Fokina ended Rafael Jodar's dream run at the Shanghai Masters on Sunday, battling back to beat his fellow Spaniard 1-6 7-6(5) 6-4 and clinch the biggest title of his career. The 25th-seeded Davidovich Fokina is set to climb 13 places to a career-high world number 13 when the rankings are released on Monday. Jodar, playing in his first Masters 1000 final and the youngest Shanghai finalist in tournament history, made a blistering start, broke for a 2-0 lead and again to take the opening set. Davidovich Fokina recovered from a break down in the second set and saved break points in three successive service games before edging a tight tiebreak to force a decider.

The momentum swung decisively in Davidovich Fokina's favour when he broke the 12th-seeded Jodar twice and sealed victory in two hours and 27 minutes. "I have a blank mind," Davidovich Fokina said. "I don't know what to say and I don't know how I feel. Just a huge relief. "After the first set I had to keep trying, keep pushing. In the tiebreak, I believed in myself again. In the third set, maybe I had a bit more fitness physically." It the third ATP singles title of the 27-year-old's career, adding to his ATP 250 triumphs in Chengdu and Mallorca this season. The first meeting between the two Spaniards pitted one of the ATP Tour's rising talents against a player enjoying the best season of his career. The 20-year-old Jodar, who was ranked outside the world's top 900 little more than a year ago, strengthened his bid to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin in his first full season on tour.

Oct 18 : Microsoft has pulled out of a data center deal with British cloud provider Nscale, Britain's Telegraph newspaper reported on Sunday. The US tech giant, one of Nscale's two largest customers, recently terminated its agreement for the data center in Loughton, Essex, according to the report. The newspaper did not specify why Microsoft withdrew from the project. Microsoft declined a Reuters request for comment. The Telegraph report said Nscale had faced repeated delays with the project. National power grid officials, it reported, had told Nscale they did not expect a power supply for the data center until the 2030s.

Nscale filed for an initial public offering in the US last month, with Microsoft and Anthropic expected to be its major customers, according to its prospectus. Nscale provides infrastructure, including compute, power and data centers, as well as software for training and running AI models.  The Nvidia-backed AI group, which competes against CoreWeave, Nebius, Crusoe and Lambda, has grown rapidly since its launch, scaling from $100 million to more than $103 billion in total contracted value in just two-and-a-half years.

GQEBERHA, South Africa Oct 18 : Australia batsman Steve Smith said he was anxious after being hit on the head and facing the prospect of another concussion after a blow playing against South Africa in the first test a week ago. Former captain Smith has previously suffered multiple concussions in his career, and he had to go through concussion protocols after a bouncer from Anrich Nortje hit him on the helmet last Monday during the second-last day of the clash at Kingsmead in Durban.  “I was a little bit anxious after the hit, to be honest,” Smith said on Sunday before the start of the second test at St George’s Park in a television interview. “It was a decent knock, and the rest of that day, I wasn't travelling too well, and I think it was more to do with anxiety, of hoping not to feel what I felt in the past, waking up the next morning and things like that.

“So, yeah, fortunately, I woke up well. I passed all the tests, and things recovered pretty quickly,” Smith added as he prepared to take part in the rain-delayed second test. The 37-year-old was assessed on the field by the physio and the doctor, and his helmet was changed as is mandatory for all such hits, but he continued his innings, scoring 27 runs as Australia built a large lead. PASSED CONCUSSION PROTOCOLS But then Smith did not take to the field at the start of South Africa's second innings on Monday, instead being subjected to the concussion protocols, which he passed. He returned from the start of the last day’s play on Tuesday to help his side to a 214-run victory and a 1-0 lead in the three-match series. Smith, who is 28 short of 11,000 test runs, was the first player replaced in a test after the introduction of a concussion substitute. He was struck on the back of the head by a Jofra Archer bouncer in the 2019 Ashes test at Lord's in London. He also suffered a concussion after being hit on the head in practice during Australia's One Day International series in England in 2020 and two months later, back home in Sydney, woke on the morning of the second ODI against India with vertigo and was sick.  There have also been incidents in Sri Lanka in 2022, at the last World Cup in India and last December in the Ashes at Adelaide where he was ruled out of the third test about 20 minutes before the toss with a vestibular issue, the sensory system located in the inner ear that controls balance and spatial orientation.

Source: Reuters
